info.title: Cecilia API
info.description: Headless organ MIDI engine. Live events are streamed over a WebSocket at `/api/v1/events` as JSON `EngineEvent` messages.

get.summary: The assistant's name, used by the MCP server (`/mcp`).
Whether a password is needed, and whether this browser is signed in.

post.summary: Sign in.
Sign out.

put.summary:
Set, change or remove the password (needs a session if one is set).
Other signed-in browsers are signed out.

get.summary: What's in the shared library.

post.summary: Add a piece from the shared library to this Cecilia's library.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Piece id in the shared library

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Organ id in the shared library

get.summary: Everything that matters (library, organs, playlists, settings) in one zip.

Every track as a MIDI file for the current organ, zipped: a backup that
any MIDI program can open.
The library as a spreadsheet (CSV).
Server identity and version.

post.summary: Import a file into the library. MIDI files may become several pieces.

parameters.description: The file's name, used to tell the format and as a default title.

parameters.description: JSON import options (`ImportOptions` for MIDI, `XmlImportOptions` for MusicXML).

post.summary:
Look inside a file before importing it: channels or staves, length,
and whether it was recorded on the current organ.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The file's name, used to tell the format and as a default title.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: JSON import options (`ImportOptions` for MIDI, `XmlImportOptions` for MusicXML).

post.summary:
Restore a backup made with `export/backup.zip`. Items with the same name
are replaced; everything else is kept. This machine's MIDI ports and
password stay as they are.

get.summary: Every track in the library, newest first.
A whole track, with its events.

put.summary: Save a whole track (from the editor or an import). Creates or replaces.

delete.summary: Delete a track (a copy is kept in the history folder).

patch.summary: Edit a track's details (title, composer, volume, verse markers…).

post.summary: Copy a track under a new name.

Download a track as a MIDI file.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: `organ` (default): the current organ's MIDI. `general_midi`: one channel per division.

get.summary: What the connected organ (the Organ out) is doing, as tracked from MIDI.

post.summary:
Operate the connected organ: draw a stop, press a key, move a pedal.
Toggle-only stops are sent only when they need to change.

get.summary: The saved port selection.

put.summary:
Save a new port selection and reconnect. Ports that could not be opened
are listed in `missing` in the response.

post.summary: Send All Notes Off and All Sound Off on every channel.

get.summary: MIDI ports currently available on this machine.
Open connections and test recorder state.

Start the raw test recorder (discards the previous test recording).
Stop test recording or playback.

Read printed music from a scan or photo with the OMR engine and return
MusicXML, ready for the usual import.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The scan's file name (PNG, JPEG, TIFF or PDF).

get.summary: Organ definitions available on this server.

Make a new organ as a copy of another (the way to start a definition for
your own instrument, e.g. from the Makin template).

put.summary:
Save changes to a user organ. If it's the organ in use, it's reloaded
everywhere straight away.

Save a playlist. Saving also marks every track as checked, clearing

get.summary: The simulator's organ, console state and audio device.

post.summary:
Do something at the simulated console: press a key, draw a stop, move a
pedal. It sounds, and the organ's MIDI is sent to the engine as input.

put.summary: Choose which organ the simulator plays (saved).

post.summary: Release all keys and push in every stop.
Check a verse entry ("4" = four verses, "12357" = exactly those).

oneOf.description: The library changed; `saved` is a newly recorded track, if any.
The service runner moved on.

AppEvent.description: Events for clients besides raw MIDI and simulator snapshots.

name.description: What the assistant is called (and, with voice control, its wake word).

duplicate_of.description: Same notes at the same times as an earlier channel (a doubled part).

polyphony.description: Average number of notes sounding together while any sound.

Confidence.description: How far a shared organ definition can be trusted.

Connection.description: How to cable the organ, in the words printed beside its sockets.

notes.description:
Anything else the organist should know before relying on this
definition (unverified numbers, settings to change on the organ...).

play_to.description: The organ's socket to play back into, e.g. "MIDI IN".

record_from.description: The organ's socket to record from, e.g. "MIDI SEQ".

expression.description: Expression per division, 0-127 (only divisions that have a pedal).

propertyNames.description:
The role of a keyboard, independent of its local name (Great, Hauptwerk,
Grand Orgue...). Order follows the English convention.

The role of a keyboard, independent of its local name (Great, Hauptwerk,
Grand Orgue...). Order follows the English convention.

stops.description: Ids of stops that are on.

oneOf.description: Load it and wait for Play (the space bar).
Start automatically this many seconds after the previous track ends.

Load it positioned at its first note and wait, so Play starts the
music at once.

Delay.description: What happens after the previous row, before this track plays.

channel.description: MIDI channel 1-16 that carries this keyboard's notes.

low_key.description: Lowest and highest MIDI note on the keyboard.

DivisionRole.description:
The role of a keyboard, independent of its local name (Great, Hauptwerk,
Grand Orgue...). Order follows the English convention.

oneOf.description: A raw MIDI message was received or sent.

allOf.description: Connections or test recorder state changed.

oneOf.description: Connections or test recorder state changed.

EngineEvent.description: Pushed to every subscriber (e.g. WebSocket clients).

oneOf.description: A speaking stop.

tag.description: Distinguishes similar stops, e.g. "Open Diapason I".

oneOf.description: Plays `source` division's stops from this stop's keyboard.
Unison off for this division.

Equivalent.description:
What a stop *is*, independent of what it's called on this organ.
Unique per `(division, equivalent)` within an organ.

on.description: true starts a fade-out, false cancels it.

Family.description: Tonal family, used to find a similar stop on another organ.

channels.description:
Channel (1-16) to division, for General MIDI files. Channels left out
are ignored. Default: the analysis's suggestions.

organ_format.description:
Read the file as the current organ's own MIDI (stops and all).
Otherwise notes are mapped by channel.

pedal_octave_up.description: Pedal notes an octave up (MuseScore writes pedal parts at 16′ pitch).

split_ms.description: Split into separate pieces at silences this long (ms). None = one piece.

title.description: Title for the piece (pieces get " (2)", " (3)"…). Default from the file.

output.description: Where the organ's MIDI goes, if anywhere.

Meter.description:
Musical framing for the score view. Exact for samples and imports;
estimated for live recordings.

bpm.description: Crotchet (quarter-note) beats per minute at 100 % tempo.

fifths.description: Key signature as sharps (+) or flats (-).

offset_ms.description: Track time of the first downbeat (after any pick-up).

gaps.description:
Silences of 4 s or more (ms from the start), where the file could be
split into separate pieces.

organ_match.description:
Share (0-1) of the file's non-note messages that the current organ
understands. High means it was recorded on (or for) this organ.

MidiConfig.description:
Which MIDI ports to use. Ports are identified by name, because OS-level port
ids are not stable across restarts or replugging.

inputs.description: Input ports to listen to (the organ console, or Hauptwerk's output).

output.description: The single output port to drive (the organ, or Hauptwerk's input).

inputs.description: Input ports that are currently open.

missing.description: Configured ports that could not be opened (unplugged, in use, renamed).

output.description: Output port that is currently open.

other_titles.description: Other hymns sung to the same tune.

path.description: Path within the library, with forward slashes.

source.description: Where it came from, for credit (e.g. "Open Hymnal Project").

password.description: The new password, or null to remove the password.

margin_start_ms.description: Silence before the first note of a new recording.

oneOf.description:
A single message that pushes in every stop (the organ's general
cancel), e.g. Johannus/Makin `F0 00 4A 4F 48 41 53 7F F7`. Organs whose
stops only *toggle* need it so playback can start from a known state.

divisions.description: Keyboards, in the order they appear (bottom to top is up to the UI).

oneOf.description: A toggle message: the receiver flips the stop's current state.
General cancel: every stop pushed in.

OrganEvent.description: Something that happened on (or should happen to) an organ console.

licence.description: Always CC0-1.0 in the shared library.

notes.description: Anything to do on the organ first ("set MIDI to mode B").

builtin.description: Shipped with Cecilia (read-only) rather than user-created.

Pattern.description: MIDI message as hex bytes, optionally with one `vv` value slot, e.g. "B1 0B vv"

start_ms.description: Start here instead of at the beginning (track ms).

oneOf.description: Default: every recorded verse once.

settle_ms.description: Wait after a general cancel on organs whose stops toggle.

oneOf.description: A track played to its end (not stopped by hand).

elapsed_ms.description: Progress through the verses being played (repeats included).

plan.description: Recorded verse numbers to be played, in order.

position_ms.description: Position in the track, in ms.

tempo.description: Playback speed in percent (100 = as recorded).

repeat.description: Start again from the top after the last row.

shuffle.description: Play the track rows in a random order.

silent.description:
Leave the stops as they are when a track ends (they're reset when the
next one starts). Otherwise every stop is pushed in at the end.

note.description: Free text shown beside the row (e.g. "Hymn 477, page 12").

track_modified.description:
The track's `modified` time when it was added or last checked,
so the UI can warn if it was edited since.

oneOf.description: Verses to play; default every recorded verse.
A heading or reminder ("Sermon", "Collection").

elapsed_ms.description: Length of the piece being recorded so far.

notes.description: Notes in the piece being recorded.

saved.description: Tracks saved since the recorder was armed.

RecordingSettings.description: How the auto-recorder splits a service into pieces.

margin_start_ms.description: Silence kept before the first note and after the last. 0-15 s.

silence_ms.description: Silence (after the last key is released) that ends a piece. 2-60 s.

Registration.description: Stops drawn plus pedal positions at one moment.

propertyNames.description:
The role of a keyboard, independent of its local name (Great, Hauptwerk,
Grand Orgue...). Order follows the English convention.

next_row.description: Row index of the track after it, if any.

row.description: Row index (into the playlist's rows) of the current track.

audio.description: Name of the audio device, if sound is available.

play.description: Start playing at once (default false: load and wait for Play).

row.description: Row to start from (default: the first track).

delay_ms.description: Pause after changing this stop before continuing playback.

full_name.description: Tooltip; defaults to the label lines joined.

id.description: Unique within the organ; stable across edits.

midi.description: Up to five ways the organ can switch this stop (jamb, crescendo, pistons...).

names.description: Up to three label lines shown on the stop, e.g. ["Open", "Diapason", "8"].

repeat_ms.description: Minimum gap between conflicting on/off messages (moving drawstops).

oneOf.description: Distinct messages for on and off.
The same message flips the stop.
One message with a value slot carrying `on` or `off`.

StopBinding.description: How a stop is switched over MIDI.

StopMapping.description: One line of "how will this track sound here".

stop.description: Stop id on this organ, or None if it is left out.

StopRef.description: A stop as a track sees it: which keyboard, and what it *is*.

invert.description: Swap text and background colours when the stop is on.

text_color.description: CSS colour of the label, e.g. "#1d4ed8".

duration_ms.description: Length of the test recording (grows live while recording).

events.description: Number of MIDI messages captured by the test recorder.

t.description: Milliseconds from the start of the track.

duration_ms.description: Where the track ends (the last note plus the end margin).

events.description: Sorted by time; at equal times, stop and pedal changes come first.

initial.description: Registration and pedals when the track starts.

organ_id.description: Organ it was recorded on (empty for samples).

verses.description: Boundaries between hymn verses, in ms. Empty = a single verse.

TrackEvent.description: Something the organist did, in organ-neutral terms.

TrackInfo.description: Descriptive fields, all editable in the library.

tempo.description:
Usual playback speed in percent (100 = as recorded). A playlist or
the tempo slider can still change it for one performance.

volume.description: Playback volume 1-100, applied through the master volume.

TrackPatch.description: Fields to change; anything left out stays as it is.

ValueBinding.description: A value-carrying control such as an expression pedal or master volume.

skip_to_last.description: When this verse ends, go straight to the last one.

stop_after_verse.description: Stop when the verse being played ends.

oneOf.description:
Play this many verses: the first ones, then the last recorded verse
(repeating the middle when asking for more than were recorded).
Exactly these recorded verse numbers, e.g. [1, 2, 3, 5, 7].

text.description: What the organist typed, e.g. "4" or "12357".

bpm.description: Crotchets per minute (from the score, or 80 if it doesn't say).
Crotchets per minute (default: the score's tempo, or 80).

streams.description:
Stream id to division; streams left out use the suggestion. Map a
stream to nothing by leaving it out and listing it in `skip`.

verses.description: Play it this many times as hymn verses (default 1).
